doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Avoiding trouble with police
summary: He learned never to argue with police, unlike friends who were jailed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Did you manage to evade any arrests or, you know trouble with the authorities yourself?

I was able, I was never, because I knew I must never argue. If I was at a party and the police arrived the first thing I would do is to tell my friends, “Let’s go.” Because I learned from the early days that you don’t argue with police. You don’t argue with them. And I saw a lot of my friends being taken to the station because they were rebels and like I said they used to cut their hairs, cut the tight pants, and the argument could escalate at the police station and that could have — and ended up many times in people serving one or two years in jail.
